originalTitle: Campaign warns of perils UK waters can pose for dogs and owners
summary: Dogs Trust points to hundreds of incidents over recent years, some involving deaths of pets or people
content: With its gentle rippling water, tall purple flowers and rustling trees, Earlswood Lakes near Solihull in the West Midlands seems the perfect spot for dogs to paddle. But their owners have been warned that the otherwise idyllic open water could prove perilous to pets. “We’ve had all this hot weather and millions of families are now spending time around open bodies of water, and it’s easy to not realise the dangers,” said Emma-Jane Thomas, rehoming manager at Dogs Trust Kenilworth during a walk around Earlswood. “Dogs love water and it’s great exercise and enrichment for them. However, not all dogs are natural swimmers,” she added. “Even strong swimmers can get into difficulties in the water.” Accompanying Thomas is Bruno the dalmatian who is clearly eager to go for a dip. But he’s been kept on a short lead. Dogs Trust has launched a new campaign with the catchline “If in doubt, keep your dog out”, in an attempt to reduce the injuries and fatalities that can occur among dogs and their owners around lakes, canals, rivers and the sea. Data from the Royal National Lifeboat Institute obtained by Dogs Trust shows that 308 dog-related incidents in open water in the UK were recorded between 2021 and 2025, almost all taking place on the coast. About a third occurred between June and September of those years. Separate figures from the National Water Safety Forum show there were 10 accidental deaths due to drowning in England between 2019 and 2025 linked to animal rescue, and 12 linked to dog walking. Data from the Canal & River Trust shows that dog-related incidents in the UK reached a five-year high in 2025, increasing by 39% compared with the previous year. Dogs Trust notes that many cases were related to dogs – or people attempting to rescue them – needing help after entering the water. Strong currents and fatigue can pose a risk, too. “When you’re thinking about open bodies of water, it’s always stop, check and think about what could be the dangers,” said Thomas, noting many are not clearly visible on first sight. “Steep banks could be an issue if a dog gets in and then swims around, [and] can’t find a way out again,” she said. “Hidden debris under the water – trolleys, broken glass, lots of weeds or branches. Blue-green algae is a danger to dogs.” Thomas also cautioned against attempting a rescue should a dog get into trouble. “If your dog’s in difficulty, it could then be two emergencies, not just one,” she said. “If you can see a safe place where your dog can exit the water, call your dog there with their recall. If you can’t do that, call emergency services and they will come and assist with dog emergencies.” Even on a picturesque summer’s day Earlswood is far from hazard-free, with a small yellow sign alerting walkers to dangers of blue-green algae. Such cyanobacteria thrive in warmer weather, forming blooms and scums – and some release toxins. “Not all blue-green algae blooms and scums are toxic, but you can’t tell just by looking at them, so it’s best to assume they are,” the Environment Agency notes. Emily Mills, veterinary projects manager at Dogs Trust, said: “Dogs can become unwell from drinking contaminated water or simply cleaning it from their fur after swimming. Symptoms can be seen as little as 15 minutes after exposure and may progress rapidly to become fatal.” Walking her rescue border collie Billy, local resident Sally said the blue-green algae was a concern – adding that Billy was always kept on a lead. “But there’s more dogs off the lead than on the lead when you walk around here. And it is a worry that there isn’t enough signage around,” she said. An online Dogs Trust survey of 2,000 owners in the UK, conducted in June, revealed that many may be unaware of such risks, with 33% reporting they did not believe blue-green algae posed a serious risk to dogs. The survey also found 19% of dog owners were unaware calm-looking water can still pose serious risks, and 80% said they’d enter water to rescue their dog, despite the risk to themselves. “Dogs love the water, we know that, and we absolutely don’t want to stop that,” said Thomas. “The reason that we’ve put the campaign out is so that owners and dogs can continue to enjoy these types of areas safely, so that when they do come here, they are aware of the risks.”
chineseTitle: 活动警告英国水域可能给狗和主人带来危险
chineseSummary: 狗信托基金指出近年来发生了数百起事件，其中一些涉及宠物或人的死亡
chineseContent: 西米德兰兹郡索利赫尔附近的厄尔斯伍德湖 (Earlswood Lakes) 拥有轻柔涟漪的湖水、高大的紫色花朵和沙沙作响的树木，似乎是狗划船的完美地点。但它们的主人被警告说，原本田园诗般的开放水域可能对宠物来说是危险的。 “我们经历了这么炎热的天气，数以百万计的家庭现在在开阔的水域周围度过时光，人们很容易没有意识到其中的危险，”凯尼尔沃思狗狗信托基金的重新安置经理艾玛-简·托马斯在厄尔斯伍德周围散步时说道。 “狗喜欢水，这对它们来说是很好的锻炼和充实。然而，并不是所有的狗都是天生的游泳健将，”她补充道。 “即使是游泳能力很强的人也会在水中遇到困难。”陪伴托马斯的是达尔马提亚狗布鲁诺，它显然渴望去游泳。但他一直保持着短暂的领先优势。狗狗信托基金会发起了一项新的活动，其口号是“如果有疑问，请将你的狗拒之门外”，试图减少湖泊、运河、河流和海洋周围的狗及其主人可能发生的伤害和死亡。 Dogs Trust获得的皇家国家救生艇研究所的数据显示，2021年至2025年间，英国公开水域记录了308起与狗有关的事件，几乎全部发生在海岸。大约三分之一发生在当年的六月至九月之间。国家水安全论坛的单独数据显示，2019 年至 2025 年间，英格兰有 10 起与动物救援有关的溺水意外死亡事件，以及 12 起与遛狗有关的意外死亡事件。运河与河流信托基金的数据显示，2025年英国与狗相关的事件达到五年来新高，与上一年相比增加了39%。狗信托基金指出，许多病例都与狗或试图营救它们的人有关，它们在进入医院后需要帮助。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
